subject: Output attribution, training-use carve-outs and feedback license — MSA / Order Form coordination
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia.park@synapsehealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@synapsehealth.com
Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on training/data-use and output rights in Order Form

Hi Markus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal and procurement reviewed the draft MSA + Order Form. Two items came up that we need explicit confirmation on before we can proceed to signature:

1) Training / model improvement: The MSA currently has a clause that allows Redwood to use customer data and outputs to improve models (Section 8.3). For Synapse’s regulated workloads we need explicit carve-outs — no training on PHI-derived prompts or outputs without prior written consent.

2) Output ownership and downstream use: Our clinical analytics team wants to confirm that Synapse retains all rights to model outputs (reports, structured data) generated by our requests and that Redwood will not re-license or use those outputs externally.

We attached our redlines (Synapse_OrderForm_v2_redlines.docx). Can someone from your contracts/legal team confirm whether you can accept these or propose alternative language?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — procurement wants to close by the end of next week.

Best,
Julia
Senior Procurement Manager
Synapse Health

Hi Julia — thanks for the clear notes and the redlines. Quick acknowledgement: we received the document and understand the two asks. Looping in Vanessa (account lead) and Neha (privacy & legal) to propose contract language that respects Synapse’s regulatory constraints.

High level from product/ops:
- We generally do not train on customer data by default for hosted tenants unless a customer opts-in; we can add explicit non-training language for regulated datasets.
- Output ownership request is common; we typically grant customers rights to use outputs and maintain customer confidentiality, but need to check the interaction with aggregated model improvement pipelines and feedback licensing.

Vanessa — can you prioritize alignment with Synapse? Neha — can you propose redline text that addresses the carve-out plus a safe feedback license that allows telemetry/metrics without exposing PHI?

-Markus

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@synapsehealth.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-30T16:15:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed redlines — non-training carve-out & feedback license (MSA §8, Order Form §2)

Julia / team — attached is a mark-up and a standalone summary. I focused on two clean, audit-friendly edits so we can avoid lengthy back-and-forth:

Summary of proposed language (high-level):
• Non-Training Carve-Out: "Notwithstanding any other provision, Redwood will not use Customer Data or Customer Outputs to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve model weights or parameter updates if such data or outputs contain Protected Health Information (PHI) or other regulated personal data, unless Customer provides prior written consent. For avoidance of doubt, telemetry and anonymized aggregate metrics may be used for system stability, monitoring, and capacity planning provided no PHI is retained."

• Output Rights: "Customer shall own Customer Outputs and any Intellectual Property therein. Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, reproduce, modify, and distribute Customer Outputs for its business purposes. Redwood shall not re-sell, publish, or otherwise commercialize Customer Outputs in identifiable form."

• Limited Feedback / Telemetry License: "Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, revocable license to use de-identified, aggregated feedback and telemetry derived from requests for the sole purposes of debugging, monitoring, and improving Redwood’s services, provided that such data does not include PHI or any data that could reasonably be re-identified."

I included optional alternative text for hosted customers who are comfortable with an opt-in training clause. Attached redline compares current draft -> proposed (redlines-comparison.pdf).

Please let me know if Tom or your legal team wants tighter definitions (we can add a short definition for PHI & re-identification risk). If Synapse wants an audit clause or SOC-2 evidence, we can include that in the Order Form as an addendum.

Attachment: redlines-comparison.pdf

-Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference
